1  Sandeep Sharma, J. (Oral)
By way of instant petition filed under Art. 226 of the Constitution of India, petitioner has prayed for the following main reliefs:
"i. That the respondents may kindly be directed to return the un- utilized/surplus land to the extent of 00-02-00 bigha to the petitioner as the same does not fall under the actual alignment and survey of Acquisition as contained in Khata-Khatauni No.
242/2332 Khasra No. 1768/1301 00-01-164 Hezct (00-04-01 Bigh) Mohal Kotadhar Tehsil Aut & District Mandi, H.P either with the lines of Section 101 of "RFCTLARR Act" or by virtue of resettlement policy made in this behalf and the other relevant rules, order and policy made thereof.

ii. That the respondents may kindly be directed to award all statutory benefits as payable under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013."

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Precisely, the facts of the case as emerge from the record, are that vide .

Notification SO No. 512(E) dated 16.2.2015, under S.31 of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter, 'Act') Government of India, Ministry of Surface Transport expressed its intention to acquire land for constructing, building (widening/four lane etc.) and the maintenance, management and operation of NH-21 in the District of Mandi.

On 15.2.2016, Central Government, in pursuance to sub-section (2)of section 3D of the Act, declared that the land specified in the Notification shall vest in Government of India, free from all encumbrances, from the date of publication.
rt Since the land of the petitioner also came to be acquired through aforesaid Notification for construction of National Highway as detailed above, he received adequate compensation.

However,
after completion of NH-21, certain land belonging to the petitioner, remained unused and as such,
on 25.7.2018, he approached respondents to return the surplus land on the return of compensation received by him in lieu of same.
However, such prayer of the petitioner was rejected by the authorities on the ground that there is no provision under the Act to return the surplus land.
In the aforesaid background, petitioner has approached this court in the instant proceedings, praying therein for the reliefs as have been reproduced hereinabove.

3. Precisely, the grouse of the petitioner as is highlighted in the petition and is further canvassed by learned counsel for the petitioner is that once it is not in dispute that some portion of land belonging to the petitioner has been rendered surplus after completion of NH, he is entitled to claim the same on payment of compensation, which he had received in lieu of the same.

To substantiate his aforesaid claim, learned counsel for the petitioner invited attention of this court to communication dated 9.12.2015 (Annexure P-7), issued by Ministry of Road .
Transport and Highways, Government of India, whereby Government of India, having taken note of the fact that there is no exclusive provision under the Act to return the land acquired thereunder,
decided to return/hand over surplus land to the State Government or administration of the Union Territory concerned, for utilization of as considered appropriate.

2 4.

Ministry of Road .
Transport and Highways, Government of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently argued that in view of aforesaid clarification issued by Government of India, National Highway Authority of rt India is under obligation to return his surplus land.

entities.text: National Highway Authority of rt India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
However, having carefully perused aforesaid communication, this court finds merit in the submission of Ms. Shreya Chauhan, learned counsel for the respondent National Highway Authority of India that vide aforesaid communication, Government of India, having taken note of the fact that there is no provision to return the land acquired under the Act, directed to return unused /surplus land to the State Government or administration of the Union Territory, for utilization of same for other purposes but definitely such land cannot be returned to the person,
from whom same was acquired.

5. Though, at this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner, while making this court peruse S.101 of the Right to Fair Compensation, Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter, 'Act, 2013'

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation, Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: ), vehemently argued that the land, whenever remains unutilized for a period of 5 years, is required to be returned to its owner, but such plea of him is devoid of merit, because the very initial lines of aforesaid provision clearly talk about acquisition of land under the Act, 2013, whereas, admittedly in the case at hand, acquisition of land was made under the National Highways Act, 1956, wherein there is no specific provision to return the unutilized/surplus land, which fact is otherwise evident from .

communication dated 9.12.2015 issued by Government of India, wherein it, while acknowledging factum with regard to land being surplus, decided to provide the same to State Government and the Union Territory, so that the same is used for other purposes, but definitely such land once acquired under the Act, cannot be of returned to the land owner, who has otherwise received compensation qua the same.
6.

At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioner argued that otherwise also on rt account of acquisition, petitioner is/was required to be provided alternative land under Rehabilitation and Resettlement Plan/Scheme but such plea of him cannot be looked into /considered in these proceedings because, in the instant case otherwise also there is no prayer in that regard, rather, for availing benefit under Rehabilitation and Resettlement Plan/Rehabilitation and Resettlement Scheme petitioner is required to be file appropriate proceedings in the appropriate court of law.

entities.text: Rehabilitation and Resettlement Plan/Rehabilitation and Resettlement Scheme
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
7. Careful perusal of S.105(3) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, clearly provides that Central Government shall, by Notification, within one year from the date of commencement of this Act, direct that any provisions of this Act relating to determination of compensation in accordance with First Schedule and rehabilitation and resettlement specified in 2nd and 3rd Schedules, being beneficial to affected party, shall apply to the cases of land acquisition under the enactments specified in Fourth Schedule or shall apply with such exceptions or modifications, that do not reduce the compensation or dilute the provision of this Act, relating to compensation, rehabilitation and resettlement as specified in the Notification, as the case may be.
.

3 8.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The Central Government vide Notification dated 28.8.2015, has provided as under:
"2. The provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition (Resettlement and Rehabilitation) Act, 2013 relating to the determination of compensation in accordance with the First of Schedule,
rehabilitation and resettlement in accordance with the Second Schedule and infrastructure amenities in accordance with the third Schedule shall apply to all case of land acquisition under the rt enactments specified in the Fourth Schedule to the said Act.
9.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition (Resettlement and Rehabilitation) Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In view of above, it is clear that the provisions of 2013 Act shall apply in land acquisition, in the afore situations only.
Consequently in view of above, this court finds no merit in the present petition and same is dismissed.
All pending applications stand disposed of.
Interim directions, if any, also stand vacated.

(Sandeep Sharma) Judge September 18, 2023 (Vikrant)
